attempts.summary: On node1, /srv/data was placed on a dedicated LVM logical volume (backed by a loop-mounted file, since the RHEL9 root disk had no volume manager). Baseline app data was written, an LVM snapshot (lv_data_snap1) was taken, the live data was then modified/corrupted/deleted, and lvconvert --merge restored /srv/data to the exact byte-for-byte baseline content (verified via sha256 checksums). A fresh snapshot (lv_data_snap_current) was left in place for ongoing recoverability, and a systemd unit (srv-data.service) ensures the loop device/VG/mount are reattached automatically on boot. Node1 was then restarted via systemctl reboot; its boot_id changed (377b5195... -> bbe2c88e...), confirming a real restart, and post-restart checks show srv-data.service active, /srv/data mounted, the snapshot LV present, and data checksums still matching the original baseline.
